say: Trilobyte turns any floor plan into measured rooms, material quantities and today's prices.
A site manager has one question: how much concrete do I order for this floor? Today that takes hours with a scale ruler, a spreadsheet and calls to suppliers.
Drop in a plan. A phone scan, a PDF, a CAD file or a BIM model.
Trilobyte finds the walls, rooms, doors and windows, reads the scale from printed areas or door widths, and measures every room.
The common questions are ready before you ask. Concrete for this floor: twenty four point three cubic metres, about forty seven hundred euros, and every room it counted is marked on the plan.
text: The common questions are ready before you ask. Concrete for this floor: 24.3 m³, about €4,700, and every room it counted is marked on the plan.

say: Prices are live. The context dot dev API searches Finnish supplier pages for concrete, levelling compound, flooring, plasterboard, paint and skirting, and each price links to its source.

say: Click a room to price it on its own. Change the slab thickness or waste, and every quantity updates.
Or ask in plain language. Laminate for the four kitchens: forty one point seven square metres, seven hundred and ninety euros.
text: Or ask in plain language. Laminate for the four kitchens: 41.7 m², €790.

say: Distance and area tools measure anything else, right on the sheet.
And every plan becomes a three D model you can orbit.
text: And every plan becomes a 3D model you can orbit.

say: On CAD and BIM drawings the geometry is exact. On held-out test drawings, area answers were right ninety nine point eight five percent of the time. On scans, the scale is estimated and flagged for a check. Other questions go to a small vision model we fine-tuned on Verda GPUs, for under two cents per thousand questions.
